subject: System Design
title: Event-Driven Invalidation
description: A fast breakdown of Event-Driven Invalidation for builders.

hook.text: A product price changes. Instead of waiting for the TTL, the database publishes a change event to invalidate the cache.

buildup.text: Event-driven invalidation uses message queues or change data capture to notify caches of data changes.

discovery.text: PostgreSQL's LISTEN/NOTIFY or Debezium can stream database changes to cache invalidation consumers.

twist.text: Events can be delayed, duplicated, or lost. The cache might still serve stale data for a brief window.

climax.text: Event-driven invalidation is faster than TTL but adds infrastructure complexity and delivery guarantees to manage.

punchline.text: Database changes trigger cache invalidation in near real time.

quiz.question: How does event-driven cache invalidation work?
options: Database changes publish events that trigger cache deletion
The cache checks the database periodically
